artifactType: Backlog 2 Batch 028 staged manual extraction input
scope: Fixed membership S4703, S2991, S3923, S3951, S4715 only
modelNote: The skill-default GPT-5.5 runner was not selectable in this delegated workspace; the available local GPT-5 Codex model was used.

checks: All five attached primary PDFs were inspected once after their local/downloaded SHA-256 hashes matched papers.primary_file_sha256.

Population layouts were selected before field staging: Total / Male / Female (S4703); Total / Match / Training (S2991); Total / U14 / U15 / U16 / U17 / U18 / U20 / Reserve (S3923); none for the two denominator exclusions.

Tabs 1-4 were staged for all three eligible studies. Every results table and usable figure was swept once for Tabs 5-10, including S4703 Figures 2-3 and Tables 1-5, S2991 Tables 1-5 plus its original-language table pages, and S3923 Tables 1-3 plus Figures 1-3.
S3951 and S4715 failed the required denominator recheck: neither reports a direct total exposure denominator or a study-specific injury rate, and rate-to-exposure derivation is prohibited.

No exposure, count, burden, or time-loss value was back-calculated from a rate. S3923 total exposure is a transparent sum of its seven directly printed, disjoint age-group exposure rows; documented structured parent rows are transparent sums of compatible direct subrows.
All staged field IDs were validated against the live extraction schema; unsupported prose and unreadable/rounded figure estimates were not forced into numeric fields.

sourceCoverage.S4703: Primary PDF pp. 1-8: abstract, registry methods/definitions, Table 1, Tables 2-5, Figures 1-3, results, illness sections, discussion and limitations checked. Figure 2 reports rounded percentages only, so no percentage-derived location counts were forced.
sourceCoverage.S2991: Merged translated-first/original-second PDF pp. 1-21: English translation pp. 1-13 and original Japanese pp. 14-21 checked; Tables 1-5, Figures 1-3, methods/definitions, results, discussion and conclusion swept. Original table values matched the translated tables.
sourceCoverage.S3923: Primary PDF pp. 1-10: abstract, methods/definitions, Tables 1-3, Figures 1-3, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion checked. Figure 1 risk-matrix points were not used where Table 3 supplied exact values.
sourceCoverage.S3951: Primary PDF pp. 1-11: abstract, methods/definition, Tables 1-3, flowchart, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion checked; only rounded group-mean game exposure is reported and no usable overall denominator/rate is available.
sourceCoverage.S4715: Primary PDF pp. 1-10: abstract, methods/definition, Tables 1-3, Figures 1-3, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion checked; exposure enters Cox models but no direct total denominator or injury rate is reported in the attached paper. Referenced supplementary material is not attached.

caveats: The paper reports 61 injuries and rounded mean match exposure by injured/uninjured group, but not a direct total at-risk denominator or injury rate.
Summing rounded group means multiplied by group sizes would be a prohibited exposure derivation, so the paper remains a fixed Batch 028 exclusion with no extraction payload.
The paper reports 54 non-contact muscle injuries and uses daily training/match minutes within recurrent-event Cox models, but it does not print a total at-risk denominator or an injury rate.
The attached primary PDF references supplementary material, but no supplement is attached; deriving incidence from model inputs is prohibited.

caveats: The strongest common line mapping is Total / Male / Female. Global registry fields stay on Total; sex-specific values occupy their matching lines.

This is a national professional-league registry paper with directly reported match-exposure rates, so it remains eligible under the league-surveillance exception even though raw match hours are omitted.

Figure 2 location percentages were scanned but not converted to counts because rounded percentages and no printed location numerators would make the derived rows less defensible than the exact diagnosis tables.

Tables 2-3 list only the ten most frequent diagnoses, so partial diagnosis sums were not written into parent tissue rows. The exact leading ankle-sprain diagnosis is retained in the generic diagnosis row.

Tables 4-5 are most-frequent-illness tables rather than exhaustive etiological distributions; direct respiratory-without-COVID and gastrointestinal rows are retained, but no broader infection total was inferred.

The source gives four unknown-mechanism injuries in addition to 18 contact and 18 non-contact injuries; no unknown-mechanism field is available.
All structured rows come directly from Tables 3-4; zero-only categories are intentionally not populated. No illness family is reported.

caveats: The strongest non-overlapping population axis is Total / U14 / U15 / U16 / U17 / U18 / U20 / Reserve. Maturity-stage rows overlap those cohorts and are therefore not mixed into the live layout.
The Total exposure values are transparent sums of the seven directly printed disjoint age-category rows in Table 1. No exposure was back-calculated from rates.
Table 2's first injury-count column sums to the paper's 235 total injuries; match counts are separately printed. Subgroup training counts were not derived by subtraction.

The Table 3 combined hip/groin row has no clean combined schema field, and the combined bone-contusion/other-bone row is broader than a bone-contusion field; both narrower mappings were intentionally left blank.

The cartilage/synovium/bursa parent row is a transparent sum of the direct cartilage-lesion and synovitis/capsulitis/bursitis subrows; its incidence and burden are direct compatible sums, while no CIs or severity means were summed.
Illness was explicitly excluded from this injury-only study. Figure risk-matrix points were not estimated where exact Table 3 values existed.
